categories.main_business_segments: Exelon operates primarily through six regulated utility subsidiaries: Commonwealth Edison Company (ComEd), PECO Energy Company (PECO), Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE), Potomac Electric Power Company (Pepco), Delmarva Power & Light Company (DPL), and Atlantic City Electric Company (ACE). Each subsidiary is responsible for the purchase, transmission, distribution, and regulated retail sale of electricity and/or natural gas within its designated service territory. Exelon itself functions as a holding company, providing centralized business services and oversight.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Exelon’s core operations center on the transmission and distribution of electricity and natural gas, utilizing advanced grid infrastructure, smart grid technologies, and energy efficiency programs. The company does not generate electricity but procures it through competitive markets and long-term contracts. Investments are focused on grid modernization, storm hardening, advanced metering infrastructure, and reliability-enhancing technologies.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Exelon’s primary customers are residential, commercial, industrial, and governmental entities within its service territories. The company serves over 10 million electric and gas customers in major metropolitan areas such as Chicago, Philadelphia, Baltimore, Washington D.C., and parts of Delaware and New Jersey. Its end markets are regulated retail energy delivery and related services.
categories.geographic_coverage: Exelon’s operations are concentrated in the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic regions of the United States, specifically in northern Illinois (including Chicago), southeastern Pennsylvania (including Philadelphia), central Maryland (including Baltimore), the District of Columbia, portions of Delaware and Maryland, and southern New Jersey. The company’s utilities collectively cover millions of customers across these densely populated areas.
categories.supply_chain_position: Exelon operates as a downstream utility, focusing on the regulated distribution and transmission of electricity and natural gas to end users. It does not own generation assets (following the 2022 separation of its generation business) and is responsible for delivering energy procured from third-party suppliers to retail customers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Exelon's strategic priorities include operational excellence, grid modernization, customer experience enhancement, and enabling clean and affordable energy choices. The company is investing heavily in infrastructure improvements, smart grid technology, and energy efficiency programs, with a strong focus on supporting state and local clean energy policies and achieving significant greenhouse gas emission reductions (50% by 2030, net zero by 2050). R&D efforts are directed toward advanced grid technologies, electrification, and supporting the integration of distributed energy resources.
categories.revenue_model: Exelon generates revenue primarily through regulated rates for the distribution and transmission of electricity and natural gas. Revenues are set by state and federal regulatory commissions and are based on cost recovery plus an allowed return on invested capital. The company also recovers costs for energy efficiency programs and other regulatory initiatives through approved riders and surcharges.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Exelon is one of the largest regulated utility holding companies in the U.S., with a leading position in its core markets. Its main competitors are other regional and national regulated utilities such as PSEG, FirstEnergy, and Dominion Energy, as well as local municipal utilities and cooperatives. Exelon differentiates itself through its scale, operational performance, and focus on clean energy transition.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the year ended December 31, 2022, Exelon reported total operating revenues of $19.1 billion and net income attributable to common shareholders of $2.17 billion. The company has a large asset base (over $95 billion in total assets post-separation) and serves more than 10 million customers. Exelon is pursuing a multi-year capital investment plan of approximately $31 billion over four years, targeting steady rate base and earnings growth.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Exelon emphasizes reliable, safe, and affordable energy delivery, industry-leading operational performance, and a commitment to supporting clean energy goals in its jurisdictions. Its value proposition includes large-scale investments in grid modernization, customer-centric programs, and leadership in enabling the clean energy transition for communities and stakeholders. The company’s scale and regulatory expertise allow it to deliver stable returns while advancing sustainability and innovation.
